Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout artifacts—including both required wake views—before touching `solver/`. I’m also consulting the fish-control bookshelf now because the prompt explicitly requires its structured transfer protocol; any mechanism it contributes will be documented with the required falsification block.

The contract confirms a single editable solver file and forbids running CFD locally. I’m anchoring the design to the sampled captures and inherited guidance next; only after the keyframes and metrics are reconciled will I select a bookshelf invariant.

The two-view sheets show self-propelled motion with a coherent alternating vortex street in both sampled controls, not advection: the wake grows behind the fish while the body translates toward the capture circle. The variants are visually almost indistinguishable until the terminal frame, so I’m now resolving the tiny score spread from trajectory, command, force, and line-of-sight data instead of treating the vortex rendering as evidence of a new route.

The inherited evidence localizes the remaining weakness to the last fraction of a beat: all four candidates capture at the same `16.0544T` step with 239 window shifts, while line-of-sight slip damping makes the best but very small improvement (`0.745869L` versus `0.745943L`) without changing the route. I’m consulting the bookshelf references now for a compact feedback mechanism that changes feasible terminal action and has a sharper falsification test than another threshold adjustment.

The assigned parent does include inherited worker logs under its sampled optimizer artifact. I found them and am folding their terminal-response hypotheses into the comparison before writing this worker’s notes; this is important because the current scalar spread is smaller than one capture step and needs provenance from the prior mechanisms.

The candidate hypothesis is now recorded before the solver edit, as required. The selected bookshelf transfer is an approach-hold invariant: preserve the traveling-wave carrier and route, then damp only measured net line-of-sight reopening inside a safe closing corridor. I’m applying that as one posterior feedback mechanism, replacing the separate terminal yaw decomposition rather than stacking another gain branch.

The durable guidance now records both sides of the evidence: target-relative slip produced the only measurable improvement, while the inherited phase-selective brake regressed and the moment lead was effectively neutral. The new solver candidate therefore uses total measured line-of-sight rate as a single terminal response signal, with the cruise and wake-producing carrier untouched. Next I’m running only the prescribed non-CFD contract and symmetry checks.

The configured check-runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable for this account (the same infrastructure issue recorded in inherited logs). I’m executing its three exact prescribed commands manually and separately so validation still covers provenance, Julia contract/schema, and editable boundaries.

All prescribed checks pass when run directly: guidance provenance, lightweight Julia policy execution, the 48/48 parameter schema, and solver boundaries. A 306,180-pair state sweep also confirms finite bounded actions, exact lateral reflection equivariance, finite observation fallback, and speed-limit anti-windup. Counterfactual replay confines the new mechanism to 18 posterior commands from `0.848L` through capture; no anterior or cruise action changes.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds bounded terminal line-of-sight-rate damping while preserving the proven carrier and route.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:257) adds the evidence-backed slip-versus-moment/phase lesson.

All prescribed non-CFD checks pass, including 48/48 parameter ownership, solver boundaries, and a 306,180-state symmetry/bounds sweep. The configured check-runner was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
